name: Holloway Commons
use: Largest dining hall on campus; the only dining hall open on weekends since fall 2025
architect: Original architect unknown; Miller Dyer Spears (2015-16 renovation), built by North Branch Construction
statusNote: The only dining hall open on weekends since fall 2025

renovations.what: 10,500 sf renovation and expansion: new roof sections, structural steel additions, HVAC, grill station, dish return, entry, elevators and two seating areas; about 365 seats added (MDS: 860 to 1,270)

facts.text: Built in 2003 as the central dining hall, replacing the Commons (now Huddleston Hall), and named for Paul Holloway, longtime USNH trustee and board chair.
The 2015-16 Miller Dyer Spears renovation and expansion raised seating from 860 to 1,270, added a grill station and improved circulation; it opened in February 2016 while the hall stayed open.
North Branch Construction's summer 2015 phase (nearly $6 million) replaced roof systems, added structural steel on several sides, and installed new HVAC, dish return, grill and entry.
The $10.5 million project added about 365 seats and a custom table made from the original hall's reclaimed railings with LED lighting.
A 4-Star Certified Green Restaurant; known for stir-fry and brick-oven specialties.
UNH consolidated weekend dining at Holloway in fall 2025 to balance the budget, closing Philbrook on weekends.

verdict: The main dining hall: a 2003 brick gable with a tall glazed bay, expanded in 2016 to 1,270 seats; busy and well run, crowded at weekends.
notes: No licensed photo found (Commons searches return only London's Holloway Road). Archives reference photo shows a tall brick gable end with a large vertical glazed window bay and chimneys. Old row's 'glass-walled terraced addition' and 'green room' descriptions come from sources I did not open; MDS confirms only a 'terrace' design theme. Ceilings 'high' and light 'strong' are inferred from the glazed gable and the MDS description, not confirmed. Seat counts differ: MDS says 860 to 1,270 (+410); TNH says +365; the old row said 883 to 1,202. Original 2003 architect unconfirmed.
judgeNotes: Archives photo only; interior judged from published descriptions.
